drivingQuestion: Are an animal running on the path and one grazing among vineyards lost property?
outcomeNote: the contradiction is resolved in the next unit

segments.he: מָצָא חֲמוֹר וּפָרָה [וְכוּ׳]. הָא גּוּפַהּ קַשְׁיָא! אָמְרַתְּ: מָצָא חֲמוֹר וּפָרָה רוֹעִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ – אֵין זוֹ אֲבֵידָה, רוֹעִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ הוּא דְּלָא הָווּ אֲבֵידָה, הָא רָצָה בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְרוֹעָה בֵּין הַכְּרָמִים הָוְיָא אֲבֵידָה. אֵימָא סֵיפָא: חֲמוֹר וְכֵלָיו הֲפוּכִים וּפָרָה רָצָה בֵּין הַכְּרָמִים – הֲרֵי זוֹ אֲבֵידָה. רָצָה בֵּין הַכְּרָמִים הוּא דְּהָוְיָא אֲבֵידָה, הָא רָצָה בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְרוֹעָה בֵּין הַכְּרָמִים – אֵין זוֹ אֲבֵידָה!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If «one found a donkey or a cow» grazing on the path, that is not deemed lost property. The Gemara asks: «This itself» is «difficult.» On the one hand «you said:» If «one found a donkey or a cow grazing on the path, that is not lost property,» from which it may be inferred that only if it is «grazing on the path it is not lost property, but» if it was «running on the path or grazing among the vineyards, it is a lost item.» On the other hand, «say the latter clause» of the mishna: If one found «a donkey with its accoutrements overturned, or a cow» that «ran through the vineyards,» that «is lost property.» From this wording it may be inferred that only if the animal is «running through the vineyards is it lost property, but» if it is «running on the path or grazing among the vineyards, it is not lost property.»

moves.summary: reisha and seifa imply opposite rulings for running on the path and grazing in vineyards
moves.about: the first clause implies running on the path or grazing in vineyards is lost; the latter clause implies it is not
